solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arranged to leave

definitions.meaning: things laid out or displayed in order have been put on view
to depart or begin a journey

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: goods displayed in order, and a traveller starting off on a journey.

clue.text: He's unwilling to give credit

parts.note: credit means belief, not a loan, so this is a doubter

explanation.definitionFit: A doubter refuses to believe or give credence to claims.

clue.text: Find path from the summit

parts.note: a track is a rough path
going down from the top

explanation.surface: Locating a trail leading down from a mountain peak.
explanation.definitionFit: To track down something is to locate it after searching.

clue.text: Horses shouldn't be, hounds may be

definitions.text: Horses shouldn't be, hounds may be

parts.words: Horses shouldn't be, hounds may be
parts.note: horses need iron on their hooves, while dogs go barefoot

explanation.definitionFit: Without shoes describes a barefoot animal, which a horse ought not to be.

clue.text: Forceful muscular types confined by surgeon

indicators.note: the surgeon's word holds the muscular types inside it, as if shut in

parts.note: a vet is a veterinary surgeon
he-men are strong muscular fellows

explanation.surface: A surgeon is surrounded by burly strongmen in a forceful scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confined by' signals the container; a vet is a veterinary surgeon, which a solver may not first think of for surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehement protest is a passionate, intense one, so forceful is a close synonym.

clue.text: It was enough for our ancestors

definitions.text: It was enough for our ancestors

parts.words: It was enough for our ancestors
parts.note: an archaic word once used to mean sufficient

explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic form meaning enough, used by earlier generations.

clue.text: One gets into a flap at its opening

definitions.text: One gets into a flap at its opening

parts.words: One gets into a flap at its opening
parts.note: getting into a flap suggests panic, but here the item has a flap at its open end that is tucked in

explanation.definitionFit: A paper sleeve for letters closes with a flap over its opening.

clue.text: Strange how mill-race ends in the lake

indicators.note: the final letter goes inside the lake's name

parts.note: Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

indicators.note: the last letter of mill-race, where it finishes

explanation.surface: An odd sight where a mill stream runs out into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes E from mill-race and 'in' places it within ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means uncanny or weird, so strange is a synonym.

clue.text: The varied uses of a classical hero

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are changed around

explanation.surface: Musing on the many uses of an ancient hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the Greek hero who slew the Minotaur.

clue.text: Pass directions around the circuit

indicators.note: the compass letters sit on either side of the circuit word, wrapping it

parts.note: ESE is east-south-east, a compass direction built from two directions
a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: Someone passes on route instructions around a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container; 'directions' is plural because east-south-east combines two compass points in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or elapse; both verbs mean to go by.

clue.text: Remain silent? No, quite the opposite

definitions.meaning: not keeping quiet means talking with someone
the reverse of something, as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to chat or talk, and the noun sense means the reverse or opposite statement.

clue.text: An upholder of the Christian word

definitions.text: An upholder of the Christian word

parts.words: An upholder of the Christian word
parts.note: upholder means supporter of belief, but literally a stand holding up the Bible

explanation.definitionFit: A reading desk in church physically holds up the Bible.

clue.text: Assume control and provide deliveries

definitions.meaning: to take charge of a business or role from someone
to carry goods across to someone

explanation.definitionFit: A buyout is assuming control of a firm; separately, bringing goods round to someone is delivering them.

clue.text: Place of secret laughter

parts.note: the idiom about laughing quietly into part of your shirt or jacket arm

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'laugh up one's sleeve' means to be secretly amused, so the garment's arm is where it happens.

clue.text: Die of cold

parts.note: die is a dice-shaped cube, not perishing, made of frozen water

explanation.definitionFit: A frozen block for drinks is shaped like a die.

clue.text: Dog-food?

definitions.meaning: a breed of dog from China

explanation.definitionFit: A chow is a Chinese dog breed, and chow is also informal slang for food.

clue.text: Gathers commodities make a lot of money in shares

definitions.meaning: accumulates supplies and keeps them in reserve

definitions.text: make a lot of money in shares
definitions.meaning: stock means shares, and piles means makes a fortune, as in making a pile

explanation.definitionFit: Hoarding supplies is stockpiling; read as two words, stock earns piles of money.

clue.text: It's clear to me, anyway, one will miss deadline

indicators.note: any way indicates the letters may be arranged in any order

explanation.surface: Someone admits they see plainly that they will not finish on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone arriving late misses the cut-off time.

clue.text: A quiet river location, well-chosen

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
the Po is a river in Italy
a site is a place

explanation.surface: A peaceful riverside spot proves a good choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite remarks are apt or relevant, so well-chosen is a synonym.

clue.text: Studies hijacking plot

parts.note: to con a text is to study it closely, so studies gives cons
piracy is seizing ships or aircraft

explanation.surface: Academic studies of hijacking reveal a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy is a secret plan or plot by a group.

clue.text: Put money on stock unit producing high market share

indicators.note: in a down clue the money word sits on top of the stock word

parts.note: cash is ready money
cows are livestock

explanation.surface: Betting money on a farm animal in hopes of good returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Business jargon for a product with a dominant market share that generates steady profit.

clue.text: Endlessly scrutinise the horses

indicators.note: the word for scrutinise loses its final letter, having no end

parts.note: to study something is to examine it closely

explanation.surface: An instruction to examine the horses without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the last letter of STUDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a collection of horses kept for breeding.

clue.text: Young female accompanists

parts.note: accompanists suggests musicians, but here they are older women who accompany girls

explanation.definitionFit: Duennas are chaperones in Spanish households who escort young women.

clue.text: Copper cost is crazy — get plaster

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters run wild and are jumbled

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: The cost of copper has gone mad, so use plaster instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used on walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Nominally commit oneself to work?

parts.note: nominally plays on writing one's name to agree to a job

explanation.definitionFit: To enlist for employment, often by signature, is the phrasal verb meaning register.

clue.text: Gin that is a mixture of bottled spirits

indicators.note: mixing the letters together signals rearrangement

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A gin cocktail blending several bottled spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a mixture of' rearranges GIN and IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Genies are spirits from folklore, often trapped in bottles or lamps.

clue.text: The problem of race

parts.note: a race here is a running event, whose hurdles and barriers make up a particular kind of race

explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is a problem or barrier, and an obstacle race is a contest over barriers.

clue.text: Lower piece of iceberg

parts.note: lower suggests the leg below the knee, and a chunk breaking off ice is named the same way

explanation.definitionFit: A mass of ice that breaks from a glacier or berg is so called, as is the back of the lower leg.

clue.text: He gets fed up with people

definitions.text: He gets fed up with people

parts.words: He gets fed up with people
parts.note: fed up literally means filled with food, here eaten from humans

explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is someone who feeds on human flesh, so people are his meal.

clue.text: Sharpness shown by man with cue, perhaps

indicators.note: signals the two words given may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A snooker player shows sharp skill at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keenness of mind, so sharpness in the mental sense is a synonym.

clue.text: Send a letter to cancel a bad debt

definitions.meaning: to send a letter requesting something
an accountant's term for removing an unrecoverable sum from the books

explanation.definitionFit: Both are phrasal verbs: sending away by post, and the accounting term for wiping out a loss.

clue.text: Goes on the stage

definitions.meaning: gets aboard a ship or train

explanation.definitionFit: Passengers board a train; theatrical slang calls the stage the boards.
